To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) tree networks have the properties of small-world networks; (b) tree networks have small-world dynamics; (c) tree networks are robust against random failures and attacks; and (d) the phylogenetic tree of the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) is a small-world network.
The small-world dynamics of tree networks can be modeled by a random walk on trees, and that this can be applied to phyloinformatics.

1) the small-world dynamics of trees can be used to identify phylogenetically relevant data in large data sets; 2) the small-world network dynamics of phylogenetic trees can be used as a basis for a phylogenetic data mining algorithm; 3) the phylogenetic data-mining algorithm is capable of identifying phylogenetically relevant information in large data sets and of extracting the phylogenetically relevant parts of the data sets, thus reducing the amount of data needed to reconstruct
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel application of data mining techniques in phyloinformatics.
the development of novel phyloinformatics methods for the analysis of large-scale data sets.
a novel approach to data mining in phyloinformatics, based on the small-world dynamics of tree networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the phyloinformatic community should not be afraid to embrace the power of the small-world dynamics of tree networks, but rather to take full advantage of it.
the small-world dynamics of phylogenetic trees are not as simple as previously thought.
the small-world phenomenon is not a property of the network structure of phylogenetic trees, but rather a consequence of the small-world dynamics of phylogenetic tree networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new method for phyloinformatics that allows us to mine for new knowledge from large data sets in a way that is not biased by our prior knowledge of the system being studied.
we have developed a new method to mine data from phylogenies and that this new method can be used to answer a wide variety of biological questions.
we have developed new methods and algorithms for phyloinformatics, the study and analysis of evolutionary trees.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tree structure of the phyloinformatics database is a small-world graph, which has a number of implications for data mining in this field.
phylogenetic tree networks provide a useful model for representing and mining phylogenetic data.
phylogenetic trees can be used to model the small-world dynamics of biological networks.
